feedback.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n}{3}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n}{3}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=-3x+1$ for $x\in [-3\pi ,3\pi ).$ The Fourier series of the $6\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{4}.$

${a}_{4}=$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the cosine coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=3\pi $ and $f(x)=-3x+1$ for $x\in [-3\pi ,3\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{4} & =\frac{1}{3\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(-3x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3\pi }x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(-3x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4}{3}x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-3x+1\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=-3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4}{3}x)\, & ⇒\,v=\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4}{3}x)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{4} & =\frac{1}{3\pi }(uv\,{|}_{-3\pi }^{3\pi }-{\int }_{-3\pi }^{3\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\pi }(\frac{3}{4}{[(-3x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4}{3}x)]}_{-3\pi }^{3\pi }-{\int }_{-3\pi }^{3\pi }\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4}{3}x)\cdot (-3)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\pi }(\frac{3}{4}[(-9\pi +1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\pi )-(9\pi +1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\pi )]+\frac{9}{4}{\int }_{-3\pi }^{3\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4}{3}x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }(\frac{1}{4}\cdot 0+\frac{9}{4}\cdot (-\frac{3}{4}){[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4}{3}x)]}_{-3\pi }^{3\pi }) \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }(-\frac{27}{16}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-4\pi )]) \\  & =-\frac{27}{16\pi }(1-1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
